answer: Auditors send each identity tightly timed nonces and record reply timestamps from several vantage points. They estimate that host's clock skew and drift; fingerprints that match too closely are merged as one machine. Extra identities on the same board cannot fake a new crystal, so a summit of scripts behind one NIC collapses to a single trace. Naive cloning therefore dies at this horizon. Limitation: a careful operator can add virtual jitter, so this only forces them onto separate machines, a glacier that cheap copy-paste farms will not climb.
